questions.fun_fact: Glance first described a blow that strikes at an angle.

questions.text: Which English word means "unwilling to spend money"?
questions.fun_fact: The origin of stingy is uncertain; it may come from a dialect form of sting.

questions.text: Which English word means "two things happening together by chance"?
questions.fun_fact: Coincidence reached English from French and is built from coincide plus -ence.

questions.text: Which English word means "money paid regularly to use a home you do not own"?
questions.fun_fact: Rent comes from Latin reddere, "to give back", through Old French rente.

questions.text: Which English word means "not letting light through"?
questions.fun_fact: The Latin source of opaque, opacus, is of unknown origin.

questions.text: Which English word means "a sudden strong urge to do something"?
questions.fun_fact: Impulse comes through French from Latin, from a root meaning "to drive".

questions.text: Which English word means "easy to break"?
questions.fun_fact: Fragile is a doublet of frail and is related to fracture and fraction.

questions.text: Which English word means "to make something clear to someone"?
questions.fun_fact: Explain comes from Latin explanare, from ex- plus planus, "flat".

questions.text: Which English word means "a short sleep during the day"?
questions.fun_fact: Nap comes from Old English hnappian, "to doze".

questions.text: Which English word means "the land along the side of a river"?
questions.fun_fact: The money kind of bank comes from Italian banca, a moneychanger's bench.

questions.text: Which English word means "money you must pay to the government"?
questions.fun_fact: Tax is a doublet of task.

questions.text: Which English word means "to make something smaller or less"?
questions.fun_fact: Reduce comes from Latin re- plus duco, "to lead".

questions.text: Which English word means "extremely tired"?
questions.fun_fact: Exhausted also means depleted of resources.

questions.text: Which English word means "to be present at an event"?
questions.fun_fact: Attend comes from Latin attendo, from ad-, "toward", plus tendo, "to stretch".

questions.text: Which English word means "a feeling that something good may happen"?
questions.fun_fact: Hope is cognate with Dutch hopen and Swedish hoppas.

questions.text: Which English word means "certain to happen and impossible to avoid"?
questions.fun_fact: Inevitable comes from Latin in- plus evitabilis, "avoidable".

questions.text: Which English word means "full of life and energy"?
questions.fun_fact: Lively is simply life plus -ly.

questions.text: Which English word means "to make something better"?
questions.fun_fact: Improve comes from Anglo-Norman emprouwer, from prou, "profit".

questions.text: Which English word means "a scientist who studies stars and planets"?
questions.fun_fact: Astronomer displaced the Old English word tungolcræftiga.

questions.text: Which English word means "a large flat area of land"?
questions.fun_fact: The noun plain, a flat area of land, is a doublet of plane, piano and llano.

questions.text: Which English word means "a sound that comes back after hitting a wall"?
questions.fun_fact: Echo comes from Greek, and may share a root with sough.

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "key"?
questions.fun_fact: Llave comes from Latin clāvis; English clef is a cognate.

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "thunder"?
questions.fun_fact: Trueno comes from Latin tonus with an extra r, influenced by tonitrus.

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "manzana" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Manzana comes from Latin mālum mattiānum, "apple of Matius", a Roman horticulturist.

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "to find out"?
questions.fun_fact: Averiguar comes from Latin vērificāre, "to verify".

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "El libro ___ sobre la mesa."?
questions.fun_fact: Estar comes from Latin stāre, "to stand", and is used for location.

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Ayer ___ mucho."?
questions.fun_fact: Llover comes from Vulgar Latin *plovere, from Latin pluere.

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "tablecloth"?
questions.fun_fact: Mantel comes from Late Latin mantēle; its doublet mandil means "apron".

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "desván" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Desván comes from Old Spanish desvanar, "to empty".

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "pillow"?
questions.fun_fact: Almohada comes from Arabic mikhadda, "pillow".

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "caber" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Caber comes from Latin capere, "to take, hold"; it is irregular: quepo, cabes.

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Ella es la chica ___ hermano es médico."?
questions.fun_fact: Cuyo comes from Latin cuius, the genitive of quī; it agrees with the thing possessed.

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Voy a ___ a mi abuela mañana."?
questions.fun_fact: Visitar comes from Latin vīsitāre, "to see, to visit".

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Soy ___ México."?
questions.fun_fact: De means "of" or "from"; Soy de... is the usual way to say where you are from.

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "pájaro" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Pájaro comes from Vulgar Latin *passarum, an alteration of Latin passer, "sparrow".

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "fork"?
questions.fun_fact: Tenedor is tener plus -dor, literally "holder".

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "estrenar" mean?

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "to usually do"?
questions.fun_fact: Soler comes from Latin solēre; it is used with an infinitive: suelo comer.

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "milk"?
questions.fun_fact: Leche comes from Latin lactis; French lait and Portuguese leite are cognates.

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Hoy yo ___ muy cansado."?
questions.fun_fact: Estoy is the yo form of estar, the verb used for temporary states like tiredness.

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "éxito" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Éxito comes from Latin exitus, "exit"; the sense shifted from "result" to "good result".

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Ella tiene ___ gato negro."?
questions.fun_fact: Un comes from Latin ūnus, "one"; it is also used before feminine nouns starting with stressed a-, as in un águila.

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "estantería" mean?

questions.text: What does the Spanish phrase "de nada" mean?

questions.fun_fact: A pesar de has a Portuguese cognate, apesar de.

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Nosotros ___ pan en el desayuno."?
questions.fun_fact: Comer comes from Vulgar Latin *comēre, a restructuring of Latin comedere.

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "sopa" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Sopa comes from Late Latin suppa, "sopped bread".

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "cuchara" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Cuchara comes from Latin cochleāre; French cuillère is a cognate.

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "to hug"?
questions.fun_fact: Abrazar is a- plus brazo, "arm", plus -ar: literally "to put arms around".

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "to be missing"?
questions.fun_fact: Faltar comes from Old Spanish faltar, "to lack".

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Yo ___ estudiante."?
questions.fun_fact: Soy is the yo form of ser; Spanish uses ser for identity, such as being a student.

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Estoy ___ casa."?
questions.fun_fact: En comes from Latin in; Estoy en casa means "I'm at home", where English says "at".

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "to be worth"?
questions.fun_fact: Valer comes from Latin valēre, "to be strong, to be worth".

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "to obtain"?
questions.fun_fact: Conseguir has many senses: to achieve, to get, to obtain, to raise funds.

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "amigo" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Amigo comes from Latin amīcus, from amō, "to love"; French ami is a cognate.

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "tomorrow"?
questions.fun_fact: Mañana also means "morning"; Old Spanish mannana was literally "tomorrow morning".

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "to sweep"?
questions.fun_fact: Barrer comes from Latin verrere; Portuguese varrer is a cognate.

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Si lo hubiera sabido, ___ venido."?
questions.fun_fact: Haber comes from Latin habēre; habría is its conditional, used for "would have".

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Por favor, ___ la puerta, tengo frío."?
questions.fun_fact: Cerrar comes from Latin serāre, "to bolt, fasten"; its stem changes e to ie.

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Espero que ___ buen tiempo mañana."?
questions.fun_fact: Hacer comes from Latin facere via Old Spanish fazer; haga is the present subjunctive.

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "never"?
questions.fun_fact: Nunca comes from Latin numquam via Old Spanish nunqua.

questions.text: Which Spanish phrase means "toothbrush"?
questions.fun_fact: Literally "brush of teeth"; cepillo alone means "brush".

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "ojalá" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Ojalá entered Spanish from an Arabic phrase; the Old Spanish form was oxala.

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "to buy"?
questions.fun_fact: Comprar comes from Latin comparāre; Italian comprare is a cognate.

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Ellos ___ español en la escuela."?
questions.fun_fact: Aprender goes back to Latin apprehendere; its doublet aprehender is a learned borrowing.

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "sensible" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Sensible comes from Latin sēnsibilis; it is a false friend: English "sensible" (reasonable) is sensato in Spanish.

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Mañana nosotros ___ a la playa."?
questions.fun_fact: Ir comes from Latin īre; its future is regular, the infinitive plus endings: iremos.

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "to forget"?
questions.fun_fact: Olvidar comes from Vulgar Latin *oblītāre, related to Latin oblīvīscor.

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "mentira" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Mentira is formed from the verb mentir, "to lie".

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Ayer yo ___ al cine."?
questions.fun_fact: Ir comes from Latin īre, but forms like voy come from Latin vādere, "to go".

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "nube" mean?
questions.fun_fact: In Spain, nube can also mean "marshmallow".

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "ventana" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Ventana comes from Vulgar Latin *ventāna; Asturian has the identical word.

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Hoy ___ lunes."?
questions.fun_fact: Hoy comes from Latin hodiē; Portuguese hoje and Italian oggi are cognates.

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Quiero ___ un vaso de agua."?
questions.fun_fact: Beber comes from Latin bibere; French boire and Italian bere are cognates.

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "¿___ te llamas?"?

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "cena" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Cena comes from Latin cēna; cenar is the verb, "to dine".

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "to pretend"?
questions.fun_fact: Fingir comes from Latin fingere; English feign and fiction are cognates.

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "disfrutar" mean?

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "zapato" mean?
questions.fun_fact: Zapato has an unknown origin shared with French sabot and Italian ciabatta.

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Es importante que tú ___ la verdad."?

questions.text: Which Spanish word means "although"?

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "enchufe" mean?

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "pegamento" mean?

questions.fun_fact: Donde comes from de plus onde, from Latin unde, "from where".

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Hay ___ flores en el jardín."?

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "sed" mean?

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "madrugar" mean?

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Llevo dos años ___ español."?

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Ellos ___ médicos."?

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "madrugada" mean?

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "Ella ___ en Madrid."?

questions.fun_fact: Lograr comes from Latin lucrārī; its doublet is lucrar.

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "despacio" mean?

questions.text: What does the Spanish word "tutear" mean?

questions.text: Spanish: which word fills the gap in "¿___ años tienes?"?

questions.fun_fact: Nadie comes from Old Spanish nade, from Latin nātī, "born (people)".

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Je ___ ai vus hier."?

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Je voudrais ___ café, s'il vous plaît."?

questions.text: Which French word means "to forget"?

questions.text: Which French phrase means "to be late"?

questions.text: Which French word means "stairs"?

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Nous ___ au cinéma ce soir."?

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "___ heure est-il ?"?

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Je ___ français."?

questions.text: What does "flâner" mean in French?

questions.text: Which French word means "umbrella"?
questions.fun_fact: Parapluie is para-, "guarding against", plus pluie, "rain".

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Mon frère ___ très grand."?

questions.text: What does "attendre" mean in French?

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Elle ___ de la musique tous les soirs."?

questions.text: What does "écureuil" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Écureuil goes back to Latin sciurus, which was itself borrowed from Greek.

questions.text: Which French word means "sidewalk"?

questions.text: Which French word means "mushroom"?
questions.fun_fact: Champignon comes from Vulgar Latin campaniolus, "grows in the field".

questions.text: In France, what meal is "le déjeuner"?
questions.fun_fact: Déjeuner is dé- plus jeûner, "to fast"; in Belgium, Switzerland and Canada it means breakfast, and lunch is le dîner.

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Elle ___ une pomme."?
questions.fun_fact: Manger comes from Latin manducare, "to chew".

questions.text: What does "sympa" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Sympa is a clipped form of sympathique, which means "nice" rather than "sympathetic".

questions.text: What does "jeudi" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Jeudi comes from Latin Iovis dies, "day of Jupiter".

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Ce sont ___ amis."?
questions.fun_fact: Possessives agree with the thing owned, not the owner: mon livre, ma maison, mes amis.

questions.text: What does "manquer" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: "Tu me manques" works backwards: it is literally "you are missing to me", meaning "I miss you".

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Je me ___ à sept heures."?
questions.fun_fact: The noun le lever also means "rising": "le lever du soleil" is the sunrise.

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Parle-___ !"?
questions.fun_fact: After an affirmative command, me becomes moi ("Parle-moi !"), but "Ne me parle pas !" keeps me.

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Je suis ___ Paris depuis trois ans."?
questions.fun_fact: The accent on à separates it from a, "has": "il a faim", but "il va à Paris".

questions.text: Which French word means "dandelion"?

questions.text: What does "poser un lapin" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: The idiom is literally "to put down a rabbit".

questions.text: Which French word means "friend"?
questions.fun_fact: Ami comes from Latin amicus, like Spanish and Portuguese amigo and Italian amico.

questions.text: In modern French, what kind of shop or place is a "librairie"?
questions.fun_fact: Librairie once meant "library"; the "bookshop" sense, from the 16th century, displaced it.

questions.text: What does "retrouvailles" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Retrouvailles is retrouver, "to find again", plus the suffix -aille, and is chiefly used in the plural.

questions.text: Which French word means "hedgehog"?
questions.fun_fact: Hérisson comes from Latin ericius, "hedgehog".

questions.text: Which French word means "snail"?
questions.fun_fact: Escargot comes from Occitan escargol; in French it is also a teasing word for a slowpoke.

questions.text: Which French word means "apple"?
questions.fun_fact: Pomme comes from Latin poma, the plural of pomum, "fruit".

questions.text: Which French word means "to be bored"?
questions.fun_fact: Ennuyer comes from Late Latin inodiare; besides "to bore", it can also mean "to annoy" or "to worry".

questions.text: What does "débrouiller" mean in French?

questions.text: What does "merci" mean in French?

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Il y a ___ chien dans le jardin."?

questions.text: Which French word means "daily"?

questions.text: What does "grenouille" mean in French?

questions.text: What does "dépaysement" mean in French?

questions.text: French: which word fills the gap in "Ils ___ leurs devoirs."?

questions.text: What does "cadeau" mean in French?

questions.text: What does "chien" mean in French?
questions.fun_fact: Chien comes from Latin canis, "dog"; it also names the hammer of a gun.

questions.fun_fact: Dormir comes from Latin dormire, and Spanish, Portuguese and Catalan still use the same form, dormir.

questions.text: Which French word means "cherry"?
questions.fun_fact: English borrowed cerise as a color name for a deep pinkish red.

questions.text: What does "pamplemousse" mean in French?

questions.text: What does "pneu" mean in French?

questions.text: What does "pomme de terre" mean in French?

questions.fun_fact: It was built with wood from an 18th-century fireplace, plus household items like shelf edging and motorbike valve springs.

questions.text: Which New York band released the 1977 debut album 'Marquee Moon'?
questions.fun_fact: The band built its following through a residency at the club CBGB in Lower Manhattan.

questions.text: In rock music, what is a 'roadie'?
options: A crew member who travels on tour
questions.fun_fact: Road crews include tour managers, lighting and guitar technicians, security, drivers and caterers.

questions.text: Which band did bassist Lemmy Kilmister found in London in 1975?
questions.fun_fact: Lemmy always insisted it was a rock and roll band, closer to punk bands than to metal.

questions.text: A rock guitarist's 'power chord' is built mainly on which interval?
questions.fun_fact: With enough distortion, a power chord produces a new fundamental an octave lower, giving a bassier sound.

questions.text: In rock music, what is a 'riff'?
questions.fun_fact: Riffs are most common in rock, punk and heavy metal, but also appear in Latin music, funk and jazz.

questions.text: Groove metal band Pantera formed in 1981 in which US state?
questions.fun_fact: Pantera began as a glam metal band and released three albums in the mid-1980s before switching to a heavier sound.

questions.text: Which drum-kit part is a pair of cymbals on a stand that close together when a foot pedal is pressed?
questions.fun_fact: Closing it makes a short 'chck' sound, while striking it open gives a shimmering wash.

questions.text: Which band's 1965 version of Bob Dylan's 'Mr. Tambourine Man' helped launch folk rock?
questions.fun_fact: The band's sound was defined by Roger McGuinn's jangly 12-string Rickenbacker guitar.

questions.text: Which band released the 1980 album 'British Steel', featuring 'Breaking the Law'?
questions.fun_fact: For 'Breaking the Law' the band used recordings of smashing milk bottles as sound effects.

questions.text: Which singer co-wrote songs with guitarist Keith Richards for the Rolling Stones?
questions.fun_fact: Before devoting himself to the band, he studied at the London School of Economics.

questions.text: Which instrument is the Fender Precision, first sold in 1951?
questions.fun_fact: It was the first commercially successful electric bass; Roy Johnson of Lionel Hampton's band was an early user.

questions.text: Which group recorded 'Rock Around the Clock' in 1954, a hit that helped bring rock and roll to a mass audience?
questions.fun_fact: Its use in the 1955 film 'Blackboard Jungle' made it an anthem for rebellious youth; it sat at number 1 on the pop charts for two months.

questions.text: Which guitarist's 1978 solo 'Eruption' showcased the two-handed tapping technique he popularized?
questions.fun_fact: Genesis guitarist Steve Hackett is widely credited with inventing two-handed tapping and influenced Van Halen.

questions.text: Which Icelandic post-rock band sometimes sings 'Hopelandic', wordless vocals that sound like Icelandic but have no meaning?
questions.fun_fact: The name means 'Victory Rose' and comes from singer Jónsi's younger sister, born days before the band formed.

questions.text: Which British band had a 1964 hit with 'You Really Got Me', built on a distorted guitar riff?
questions.fun_fact: The song reached number one on the UK singles chart in September 1964, the month after its release.

questions.text: Who is nicknamed 'The King of Rock and Roll'?
questions.fun_fact: His first RCA Victor single, 'Heartbreak Hotel', came out in January 1956 and went to number one in the US.

questions.text: What does a guitar's whammy bar, also called a tremolo arm, change?
questions.fun_fact: It enabled the 1980s shred-guitar 'dive bomb' effect, in which a note drops sharply in pitch.

questions.text: Which guitarist is nicknamed 'Slowhand'?
questions.fun_fact: The nickname puns on the 'slow handclap' of an audience waiting while he replaced a broken string.

questions.text: Tom Scholz, who founded Boston and wrote 'More Than a Feeling', studied engineering at which university?
questions.fun_fact: After Boston's success he founded a company that sold his inventions under the Rockman brand.

questions.text: Which British band released the 2000 debut album 'Parachutes', featuring 'Yellow'?
questions.fun_fact: 'Parachutes' came out on Parlophone in the UK in July 2000 and on Nettwerk in the US that November.

questions.text: The Cure formed in 1976 in which English town?
questions.fun_fact: The group first called itself Malice before later changing names and settling on The Cure.

questions.text: Which band did Buddy Holly lead on 1957 hits such as 'That'll Be the Day'?
questions.fun_fact: The Beatles chose their own name partly in homage to the Crickets.

questions.text: Which Irish band released the 1991 shoegaze landmark 'Loveless'?
questions.fun_fact: The album was recorded at 19 different studios, with costs rumored to have reached 250,000 pounds.

questions.text: In which country was AC/DC guitarist Angus Young born?
questions.fun_fact: His family flew from Scotland to Sydney in June 1963, when Angus was eight years old.

questions.text: How many strings does a standard electric guitar usually have?
questions.fun_fact: Seven-string guitars add a low B string below the usual low E, and eight-string guitars add yet another.

questions.text: Which rock and roll pioneer wrote and recorded 'Johnny B. Goode'?
questions.fun_fact: Berry's recording is on the Voyager Golden Record, sent into deep space aboard both Voyager spacecraft launched in 1977.

questions.text: Which Canadian singer-songwriter, backed by Crazy Horse, earned the nickname 'Godfather of Grunge'?
questions.fun_fact: Nirvana and Pearl Jam cited his distorted guitar style, and he made 'Mirror Ball' with Pearl Jam in 1995.

questions.text: Which French metal band took its name from the Japanese name of Godzilla?
questions.fun_fact: Gojira was the first heavy metal band to perform at an Olympics opening ceremony, at the 2024 Summer Games in France.

questions.text: Which company introduced the Stratocaster electric guitar in 1954?
questions.fun_fact: It was designed by Leo Fender with colleagues including Bill Carson, Rex Gallion, George Fullerton and Freddie Tavares.

questions.text: Oasis, led by brothers Liam and Noel Gallagher, formed in which English city in 1991?
questions.fun_fact: The first line-up was Liam Gallagher, Paul 'Bonehead' Arthurs, Paul 'Guigsy' McGuigan and Tony McCarroll; Noel joined a few months later.

questions.text: Which shock-rock singer, born Vincent Furnier, had a hit with 'School's Out'?
questions.fun_fact: Alice Cooper began as a band in Phoenix, Arizona; Furnier legally took the name for his solo career in 1975.

questions.text: Which guitar maker first sold the Les Paul electric guitar in 1952, naming it after a famous guitarist?
questions.fun_fact: It was designed by Gibson factory manager John Huis and his team, with input from and endorsement by Les Paul.

questions.text: Who was the lead vocalist of Queen?
questions.fun_fact: Before music he studied graphic art and design at Ealing Art College, and later designed the band's crest.

questions.text: Which Led Zeppelin guitarist played his guitar with a bow on live versions of 'Dazed and Confused'?
questions.fun_fact: Page used a cello bow, a technique he developed in his days as a session musician.

questions.text: Which band recorded the 1981 song 'Don't Stop Believin''?
questions.fun_fact: The song is unusual because its true chorus does not arrive until the song is nearly over, with about 50 seconds left.

questions.text: The hard rock band Scorpions, known for 'Rock You Like a Hurricane', comes from which country?
questions.fun_fact: The band was formed in Hanover in 1965 by guitarist Rudolf Schenker.

questions.text: Which singer, formerly of Rainbow, became Black Sabbath's lead vocalist in 1979?
questions.fun_fact: He sang on three Sabbath studio albums: 'Heaven & Hell', 'Mob Rules' and 'Dehumanizer'.

questions.text: Which New York punk band's members all took the stage surname 'Ramone'?
questions.fun_fact: They took the idea from Paul McCartney, who used the stage name Paul Ramon in the Beatles' early days.

questions.text: Sepultura, formed in 1984 by the Cavalera brothers, came from which Brazilian city?
questions.fun_fact: The band signed with Roadrunner Records in 1988, which helped launch its international career.

questions.text: In which Mississippi town was Elvis Presley born in 1935?
questions.fun_fact: His family moved to Memphis, Tennessee, when he was 13, and he began recording at Sun Records in 1954.

questions.text: Which Sheffield band released the 2006 debut album 'Whatever People Say I Am, That's What I'm Not'?
questions.fun_fact: It became the fastest-selling debut album in British chart history at the time.

questions.text: Which rock and roll pioneer recorded 'Tutti Frutti' and 'Long Tall Sally' in the mid-1950s?
questions.fun_fact: He was part of the first group inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1986 and is called the 'Architect of Rock and Roll'.

questions.text: In which US city is the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame museum located?
questions.fun_fact: The museum building was designed by architect I. M. Pei and dedicated on September 1, 1995.

questions.text: Which musician, known for the 1986 hit 'Nothing to My Name', is dubbed the 'Godfather of Chinese Rock'?
questions.fun_fact: He began his career as a classically trained trumpeter before switching to guitar.

questions.text: Metallica, Megadeth, Anthrax and which other band make up the 'Big Four' of American thrash metal?
questions.fun_fact: German thrash has its own 'Big Teutonic Four': Kreator, Destruction, Sodom and Tankard.

questions.text: Which design student created the Rolling Stones' tongue-and-lips logo in 1970?
questions.fun_fact: He was paid just 50 pounds at first, plus 200 more in 1972; the band bought his copyright for 26,000 pounds in 1984.
